questions.q: Even when a user saves a single record through the UI, how does Trigger.new represent that record inside the trigger?
options: As a single SObject, not a list
As a list containing exactly one item
As a map keyed by record Id
Trigger.new is not populated for single-record saves
questions.explain: Trigger.new is always a list, even for a single-record save — which is exactly why bulk operations can hand a trigger 200 records in that same list at once.

questions.q: Why does a trigger with a SOQL query inside a for loop over Trigger.new pass a single-record test but fail against a 200-record bulk insert?
options: With one record, the loop issues only one query, which is fine; with 200 records it issues 200 queries, which can exceed the per-transaction SOQL limit
Single-record tests use different governor limits than bulk tests
Apex triggers cannot process more than one record without an explicit bulk flag
The loop only executes on even-numbered record counts
questions.explain: SOQL-in-a-loop issues one query per record in Trigger.new — with a single record that's one query (fine), but with 200 records it's 200 queries, which can breach the synchronous 100-query-per-transaction governor limit.

questions.q: In the bulk test example, why does insert accounts (a single DML statement on a list of 200 records) matter for proving bulk safety, as opposed to inserting them one at a time in a loop?
options: It doesn't matter — inserting one at a time in a loop would prove the same thing
Inserting in a loop is faster and therefore preferred
A single DML statement on all 200 records fires the trigger once with all 200 in Trigger.new, which is what actually exercises the bulk code path
Apex does not allow inserting more than 50 records in a single statement
questions.explain: Inserting all 200 records in one DML statement fires the trigger exactly once with all 200 in Trigger.new simultaneously — inserting them one at a time in a loop would fire the trigger 200 separate times with one record each, never exercising the actual bulk code path.

questions.q: Besides testing a large batch like 200 records, what other record counts does this lesson recommend testing a trigger against?
options: Only ever test with exactly 200 records
Only negative record counts
Record counts are irrelevant as long as assertions are present
Exactly 1 record and 0 records (an empty list), to catch regressions in the simple path and edge cases
questions.explain: A rigorous trigger test suite also checks the normal single-record case and an empty list, to make sure the bulk-safe rewrite didn't break the simple path or throw on empty input.

questions.q: What is the general fix for a trigger handler that issues a SOQL query inside a loop over Trigger.new?
options: Remove all SOQL queries from the trigger entirely
Collect the relevant Ids into a Set first, then issue a single bulk SOQL query (often into a Map) outside the loop
Wrap the loop in a try/catch block
Reduce the trigger's batch size to 1
questions.explain: The bulk-safe pattern collects the Ids needed across all records first, then issues one SOQL query (commonly building a Map) outside the loop, instead of querying once per record inside it.
